trusted_external_entities.name: Ethereum Client
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The Ethereum client calling EVMC modules is a trusted component of the same node. However, EVMC modules should still validate inputs as the client may pass malformed data due to bugs. Trust is based on being part of the same software stack with shared security context.

trusted_external_entities.name: Smart Contract Verifiers
trusted_external_entities.rationale: On-chain contracts verifying merkle proofs are arbitrary third-party code. They rely on stable merkleization but could be malicious or buggy. Proofs must be validated cryptographically regardless of contract behavior.

trusted_external_entities.name: Hardware Wallet Implementations
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Hardware wallets verifying merkle proofs are external devices with limited upgrade capability. They implement verified cryptographic operations but may lag behind protocol changes. Trust is conditional on proper implementation of SSZ merkleization.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Gossip Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P gossip network is the source of serialized SSZ data. Any network participant can inject malformed or malicious data. All received data must be validated against length limits and schema before processing.

trusted_external_entities.name: Off-Chain Verifier
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External verifiers validating merkle proofs without full state are anonymous third parties. They may submit invalid proofs or attempt to exploit proof verification logic. All proofs require full cryptographic validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External user or application submitting transactions with access lists. Transaction data is arbitrary and could contain malicious access list entries. All access list entries must be validated and gas costs properly calculated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Other Ethereum nodes propagating blocks via P2P network. Peers are anonymous and may propagate invalid blocks or attempt eclipse attacks. All received blocks must be fully validated before acceptance.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Client passes well-formed EVMC messages. Module validates message type is EVMC_CALL, destination is in precompile range, and no code is provided before execution.
Merkle proofs must be verified against known state roots. Generalized indices must be stable across forks via ProgressiveContainer. Invalid proofs must be rejected.
Hardware wallets verify proofs using embedded merkleization logic. Stable generalized indices ensure proof compatibility across upgrades. Wallets may not support newest fork features immediately.
Serialized SSZ data from P2P must have length validated before full decoding. ProgressiveLists require runtime length limits to prevent DoS. Malformed data must be rejected early.
Off-chain verifiers submit proofs for validation without full state. Proofs must be cryptographically verified. Computed roots must match expected state roots.
User-submitted transactions with access lists must have entries validated. Gas costs for access list must be correctly calculated. Malformed access lists must be rejected.
Blocks propagated by peers must be fully validated including header, transactions, and state transitions. Invalid blocks must be rejected without affecting node state.
